title: Voice Memo While Tapering Off Medication I've Taken for Years
script: Narrator: [uncertain] Recording this on week three of tapering, mostly to have some honest account of a process everyone around me insists on narrating as unambiguously triumphant.
Narrator: [honest] It doesn't feel triumphant, particularly. It feels like slowly removing scaffolding from a structure nobody's entirely certain can stand unassisted yet.
Narrator: [reflective] Eight years on this medication, long enough that I've genuinely forgotten which version of my temperament belongs to the drug and which belongs, more fundamentally, to me.
Narrator: [thoughtful] That's the part nobody adequately prepares you for, the unsettling ambiguity of not knowing where the treatment ends and the actual self quietly resumes.
Narrator: [uneasy] Friends keep asking whether I feel more like myself now, a question I find myself unable to answer honestly, since I no longer possess a reliable baseline to compare against.

Narrator: [wry] There's an irony here I can't quite escape: the medication that once rescued me from a version of myself I couldn't tolerate has become, itself, a version I'm now cautiously testing whether I can tolerate leaving.
Narrator: [honest] My psychiatrist has been admirably unhurried about this, refusing to frame it as either victory or defeat, merely as information we're gathering carefully, together.
Narrator: [thoughtful] She reminded me that tapering successfully doesn't retroactively mean the medication was unnecessary, a reframe I've had to return to more than once already this week.
Narrator: [reflective] Some days the anxiety resurfaces with a familiarity that frightens me, an old visitor I'd assumed had permanently relocated elsewhere.
Narrator: [determined] Other days pass almost unremarkably, which itself feels like a small, quiet victory I'm learning not to over-interpret in either direction.
Narrator: [warmly] I've stopped asking whether I'll eventually be entirely medication-free, and started asking, instead, whether whatever configuration I land on actually lets me live well.
Narrator: [peacefully] That's a considerably more modest question than the one I started with, and, I'm slowly discovering, a considerably more honest one too.
